nodes.title: RAFT / generic 2-input DNN flow
widgets_values:
RAFT OPTICAL FLOW THROUGH THE GENERIC cv2.dnn NODES

THE MODEL'S CONTRACT, all measured on this OpenCV 5.0.0 build:
  * two network inputs named '0' and '1', each (1, 3, 360, 480) float32 RGB
    at 0-255 - there is NO 1/255 scaling, hence input_scale = 1.0.
  * 360x480 is BAKED IN: 320x240, 640x360 and 496x368 all assert inside
    reshape2_layer. The subgraph resizes into the net and scales the flow
    VECTORS back out (x by src_w/480, y by src_h/360).
  * it returns the flow TWICE - full resolution and 1/8 - and the layer ORDER
    FLIPS BETWEEN ENGINES, so the field is picked by SHAPE
    ('4-D map (highest resolution)'), never by index or 'last'.
  * THE NaN, and the retry that answers it. For SOME input pairs the model
    returns NaN - all of it, or 83% of it with the rest still CORRECT,
    which looks like a field with holes. It is NOT simply 'large motion':
    blurred noise survives 12-96 px shifts, a photo NaNs at 24 px and is
    fine at 32/48/64/96, and two frames of the pedestrian clip 24 apart
    (0.84 px of median motion) come back all-NaN. Deterministic per pair.
    This used to be pinned away with ENGINE = CLASSIC, which was finite on
    every case tried and matched the default engine to 4.2e-5 px for +22%
    time. OPENCV 5.1 DELETED THAT ENGINE: the enum is now AUTO / OPENCV /
    ORT, ENGINE_OPENCV *is* the old 'new graph' engine, and this build has
    WITH_ONNXRUNTIME=OFF so ORT falls back to it too - all three labels are
    one code path, bit for bit (identical output order, identical timing,
    array_equal tensors). There is nothing left to pin.
    So the blueprint recovers the field instead: 'Is the field finite?'
    (cv2.checkRange) drives an If/Else Switch, and on NaN a SECOND forward
    runs the pair in the OTHER order and negates the result. Measured: 6 of
    9 NaN pairs come back, exactly - the pan-32 clip returns -48.05 against
    a truth of -48.0. The If/Else branch is lazy, so the second forward
    only costs anything on a pair that failed. A cv2.patchNaNs guard still
    sits behind the switch for the 3 pairs neither direction answers.

    WATCH OUT when judging this workflow by eye: it feeds CONSECUTIVE
    frames (0 and 1), which is one of the pairs that never NaNed on any
    engine. A plausible-looking flow here says nothing about the bug -
    frames 0 and 24 of the same clip are the ones that trigger it.

WHAT MAKES THIS GENERIC: 'DNN Forward All' splits the blob's batch dimension
across the names in input_names, so ANY 2-frame model runs through the same
one-preprocess chain. To swap one in, change model / net_width / net_height /
input_names / input_scale on the subgraph - there is nothing to rewire.

Row 1 RAFT, row 2 DIS on the same pair, row 3 where they disagree.


DEV NOTE: HOW IT SCORES 
(exact ground truth, tests/synthvideo.py, 320x240,
5 camera cases x 3 pairs; the full table is in the README):
                         endpoint err (bg)   motion-seg IoU   s/pair
  RAFT                          0.071             0.682        1.45
  DIS finest_scale=0            0.279             0.596        0.009
  DeepFlow                      0.202             0.504        0.108
RAFT is 4x more accurate on the background and 160x slower. It does NOT help
frame interpolation (2.40 vs 2.36 mean abs error - two-sided warping plus a
cross-fade absorbs the difference), so the shipped video blueprints keep DIS.

nodes.title: Frame A + frame B = one 2-frame batch
Forward (batch split across the named inputs)
The FULL-RES flow (order is not stable!)
magnitude + angle (same slots as the DIS node)
RETRY: frame B first (the reverse pair)
Forward the reverse pair (only when the first NaNs)
The FULL-RES flow (order is not stable!)
Is the field finite? (NaN fails checkRange)
Finite? keep it. NaN? take the reversed pair
